topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by outlining the main themes and learning objectives regarding cellular transformation, cancer genetics, and genomic instability.

topics.label: Viral origins of oncogenes and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the discovery of transforming tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental assays to measure oncogenic transformation.

topics.label: Functional classification of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated mutations and illustrate their mechanistic effects on cell cycle checkpoints and protein function.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the distinct forms of sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer alongside the specific DNA repair, replication, and mitotic defects that generate them.

topics.label: Stepwise tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step accumulation of mutations during tumorigenesis and how inherited genetic defects accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture wrap-up, offering recommended reading and looking ahead to the next session.
